wordings.MODEL_DESCRIPTION: A decoder transformer released by DeepSeek in December 2024 with open weights. Each layer is multi-head latent attention followed by a feed-forward sublayer, which is a dense multi-layer perceptron in the first D layers and the DeepSeek mixture of experts in every later layer. The sizes are those of config_16B.json of the released inference code, which the hand-drawn diagram draws: 27 layers of width 2048 with 64 routed experts. The released 671B model runs the same code at larger sizes.
wordings.EMBEDDING_DESCRIPTION: The token identifiers of the prompt, one per position, each an entry of a vocabulary of 102400 tokens. The embedding E holds one learned vector of m = 2048 values for every token and returns the vector of the token at each position.
wordings.DENSE_LAYER_DESCRIPTION: The first D = 1 layers. Each layer applies multi-head latent attention and then the dense multi-layer perceptron, each after an RMSNorm and inside a residual connection.
wordings.MOE_LAYER_DESCRIPTION: The L = 26 later layers, each with weights of its own, which with the D dense layers make the 27 layers of the model. Each layer applies multi-head latent attention and then the DeepSeek mixture of experts, each after an RMSNorm and inside a residual connection.
wordings.RESIDUAL_DESCRIPTION: The RMSNorm of the hidden state is passed through the sublayer, and the output of the sublayer is added to the hidden state as it arrived.
wordings.ATTENTION_DESCRIPTION: The keys and the values of every head are projected from one latent of 512 values per token, so a cache of generated tokens holds the latent and one rotated key of 64 values per token, where standard attention holds a key and a value for every head. Each of the h = 16 heads has a query and a key of d = 192 channels, of which d_n = 128 carry no position and d_r = 64 are turned by the rotary embedding. The rotated part of the key is shared by every head. The scores are masked causally, and the weighted values of the heads are mapped back to the model width by W^O.
wordings.QUERY_GENERATION_DESCRIPTION: The query of every head, projected directly from the hidden state, because config_16B.json sets no low rank for the queries. W^Q gives the d_n channels that carry no position, and W^QR gives the d_r channels the rotary embedding turns. The two runs are laid end to end as the d channels of the query.
wordings.KV_GENERATION_DESCRIPTION: W^DKV projects the hidden state to a latent of l = 512 values, which an RMSNorm normalises. W^UK and W^UV project the latent to the key channels that carry no position and to the values of every head. W^KR projects the hidden state to the d_r channels of the key the rotary embedding turns, and those channels are repeated for every head. The two runs of the key are laid end to end as its d channels.
wordings.ROTARY_DESCRIPTION: The d_r channels read as d_r / 2 complex numbers, each multiplied by the entry the YaRN table holds for its position and its pair, and written back as channels. The table holds e^(i p theta'_j) for position p, where theta_j = beta^(-2j / d_r) is the angular velocity of pair j with beta = 10000, and YaRN divides the angular velocity of the slow pairs by kappa = 40. The released code applies YaRN whenever its maximum sequence length, 16384 by default, exceeds the 4096 tokens of the original training context.
wordings.CORE_DESCRIPTION: Each query takes the dot product with the key of every earlier token and of its own token over the d channels. The scores are multiplied by the inverse square root of d and by mu squared, the attention factor YaRN adds, and a softmax over the slots turns them into weights. Each query returns the sum of the values under those weights.
wordings.MLP_DESCRIPTION: The dense feed-forward network of the first layers, a SwiGLU with an inner width of u = 10944. W_1 and W_3 project the token to u values each, the sigmoid linear unit is applied to the first, the two are multiplied, and W_2 maps the product back to m.
wordings.MOE_DESCRIPTION: A mixture of n = 64 routed experts, of which each token reads k = 6, and S = 2 shared experts, which every token reads. The gate scores the routed experts, keeps six, and normalises their scores into weights. The output is the sum of the six routed experts under those weights, added to the output of the shared experts.
wordings.GATE_DESCRIPTION: W^g scores each of the n experts for a token, and the sigmoid maps each score into the interval from 0 to 1. The Top k keeps the six highest, and the kept scores are divided by their sum, so the weights of the six chosen experts sum to one. The sigmoid is monotone, so the same six experts hold the highest scores whether the selection stands before or after it.
wordings.ROUTED_EXPERTS_DESCRIPTION: Each chosen expert is a SwiGLU with an inner width of f = 1408. Each projection holds the weights of all n experts and reads those of the expert each slot chose, and the view named Diagonal keeps the output of that expert.
wordings.SHARED_EXPERTS_DESCRIPTION: The two shared experts, which every token reads, held as one SwiGLU whose inner width s = S f = 2816 is the sum of theirs.
wordings.OUTPUT_DESCRIPTION: The final RMSNorm is applied to the hidden state of every position, and the head projects it to one score for each of the 102400 tokens of the vocabulary. The released forward pass keeps the last position alone during generation, and a sampler turns its scores into probabilities.
wordings.EMBEDDING_OPERATOR_DESCRIPTION: A table lookup. The embedding holds one learned vector of m values for every token of the vocabulary, and it returns the vector of the token each position holds.
wordings.PAIRS_AS_COMPLEX_DESCRIPTION: Every two adjacent channels read as one complex number, the first as the real part, as torch.view_as_complex reads them.
wordings.DECOMPLEX_DESCRIPTION: Each complex number written back as two adjacent real channels, the real part first, as torch.view_as_real writes them.
wordings.TOP_K_DESCRIPTION: The six highest of the n expert scores of each token are kept, on the axis k/n, whose live positions are the six chosen experts. The score of every other expert is the unit, which the normalisation that follows ignores.
wordings.CONCATENATE_DESCRIPTION: Two runs of channels laid end to end on one axis, the channels that carry no position first and the rotated channels after them, which is torch.cat along the last dimension of the released code.
wordings.SILU_ROLE: The sigmoid linear unit, x sigma(x), applied to every value of the first projection on its own. Its product with the second projection is the gating of the SwiGLU.
wordings.SIGMOID_ROLE: The logistic sigmoid of every expert score, which the configurations whose score function is sigmoid apply before the selection.
wordings.SCORE_SCALE_ROLE: Every score multiplied by the inverse square root of d = d_n + d_r and by mu squared, with mu = 0.1 m_c ln(kappa) + 1 for the configured factor m_c = 0.707 and the YaRN factor kappa = 40.
wordings.QUERY_ROLE: The query projection of the channels that carry no position, from m to d_n channels per head.
wordings.ROTARY_QUERY_ROLE: The query projection of the channels the rotary embedding turns, from m to d_r channels per head. The released wq holds this projection and the one of W^Q as one weight whose output is split.
wordings.LATENT_ROLE: The down projection of the hidden state to the key-value latent of l values. The released wkv_a holds this projection and the one of W^KR as one weight whose output is split.
wordings.ROTARY_KEY_ROLE: The projection of the hidden state to the d_r key channels the rotary embedding turns, shared by every head.
wordings.KEY_ROLE: The up projection of the latent to the key channels that carry no position, d_n per head. The released wkv_b holds this projection and the one of W^UV as one weight whose output is split.
wordings.VALUE_ROLE: The up projection of the latent to the values, d_v per head.
wordings.OUTPUT_ROLE: The output projection, which maps the h heads of d_v values back to the m values of the model width.
wordings.GATE_ROLE: The gate projection, which gives every token one score per routed expert.
wordings.FIRST_PROJECTION_ROLE: The first projection of a SwiGLU. The sigmoid linear unit is applied to its output.
wordings.THIRD_PROJECTION_ROLE: The third projection of a SwiGLU, which multiplies the output of the first.
wordings.SECOND_PROJECTION_ROLE: The second projection of a SwiGLU, back to the model width m.
wordings.HEAD_ROLE: The head, which gives every position one score per token of the vocabulary.
wordings.RMS_NORM_ROLE: The root-mean-square normalisation divides the values of a vector by their root mean square and multiplies each by a learned weight.
wordings.YARN_TABLE_ROLE: The table of the rotary embedding over the positions and the d_r / 2 pairs, with the YaRN frequencies.
wordings.MASK_VIEW_DESCRIPTION: Slot w of token x reads the key or the value of token x - w, so slot 0 is the token itself and slot w is the token w before it. A slot before the first token names a negative position, and a read outside an axis holds the unit, which the softmax and the weighted sum ignore. The slot axis has the length of the sequence, so each token reads itself and every token before it and never a later one, which is the set the causal mask of the released code leaves. The slot axis leaves the view as w|x.
wordings.DIAGONAL_VIEW_DESCRIPTION: The output W_2 gives for every routed expert at every slot, read where the expert is the one the slot chose. The projection holds the weights of all n experts, and the diagonal keeps the output of the chosen one.
